summary: Validated the 3 NEW features (Bulk Triage, Evaluation Dashboard, Rerun Diff) end-to-end on backend + frontend. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py (10 pytest cases, 10/10 PASS in 4.5s) covering: bulk-review by taxonomy, bulk-review by ids, support RBAC 403, bulk_* audit event write, invalid action 400, /benchmark/{id} returns has_truth+precision=100+match_recall=100+exception_recall=100+F1=100+FP=0 with all 3 gates green for the seeded demo batch, /benchmark returns full score array, unknown batch 404, /batches/{id}/rerun with SAME policy yields total_changes=0/regressed=0 (idempotent), stricter policy (amount_tolerance_paise=0) triggers regressed>0, and policy is restored to 100 paise after the test. Also re-ran the existing regression suite (backend_test.py) — 18/18 PASS. Playwright drove analyst login → Evaluation page (screenshot confirmed AUTO-MATCH PRECISION 100%, MATCH RECALL 100%, EXCEPTION RECALL 100%, F1 100%, 36 TP / 0 FP / 0 FN / 45 labelled records, all 3 gates green, 9-row cross-batch trend table) → /batches: ran a fresh demo, clicked rerun-btn-{id} which navigated to /audit?diff=1&base=..&compare=.. (URL confirmed) → Audit Rerun Diff tab rendered diff-base-select + diff-compare-select + Total/Resolved/Regressed/Other=0 summary + 'No differences — reruns are identical (idempotent)' → /exceptions grouped by taxonomy showed 5 bulk-resolve + 5 bulk-escalate buttons + bulk-note-input; typing a note + clicking bulk-escalate-MISSING_IN_BANK produced 3 ESCALATED pills, then clicking bulk-resolve produced 3 RESOLVED pills with toast '2 case(s) resolved'. All three features working as spec.

In /api/exceptions/bulk-review, when only `ids` is provided the query still requires batch_id (fine) but silently ignores ids belonging to a different batch. Consider validating that all supplied ids belong to the given batch_id.
Bulk review writes ONE audit event with entity_id = taxonomy OR literal 'selection' when using ids. For traceability, consider recording the affected id list (or count only, if PII/size concerns).
